rubrics.rubric: Does the Bank Reconciliation sheet reconcile the Q1 bank activity to the books and investigate every unmatched bank transaction?
criterion: The sheet starts from the bank ending balance supported by Bank_Statement_Q1_2024.csv.
Reconciling items are quantified.
The adjusted bank balance is compared with the GL cash balance or the documented absence of cash-account entries.
The discrepancy-investigation table includes bank Reference.
The discrepancy-investigation table includes bank date.
The discrepancy-investigation table includes amount.
The discrepancy-investigation table identifies the GL match or states no GL entry.
Every bank transaction without a matching GL entry has a source-grounded explanation or an explicit unresolved investigation status.
Bank-versus-GL differences are quantified at the transaction level, category level, or both, and the chosen presentation supports completeness and materiality.
Material discrepancies are ranked without relying on an arbitrary exception count.

rubrics.rubric: Does the Adjusting Journal Entries sheet provide complete, balanced, source-grounded entries that bring the books into agreement?
criterion: Each journal-entry line contains Entry number.
Each journal-entry line contains Date.
Each journal-entry line contains Account Number.
Each journal-entry line contains Account Name.
Each journal-entry line contains Debit and Credit.
Each journal-entry line contains an explanation.
Each bank-related journal entry identifies the bank Reference.
Debits equal credits within each entry.
Account selections are consistent with the chart of accounts or are clearly labeled provisional clearing accounts.
Proposed entries distinguish confirmed corrections from items requiring additional evidence.

rubrics.rubric: Does the Vendor Payment Audit completely and accurately cross-reference the Q1 vendor-related bank withdrawals against the AP subledger?
criterion: Every Q1 vendor-related check and EFT in the bank statement appears in the cross-reference.
The cross-reference contains every required column from Bank Reference through Notes.
Matches are based on the AP and bank source fields rather than an unsupported invoice assumption.
Matched withdrawals identify the corresponding APID.
Status conflicts between the bank and AP subledger are labeled Status discrepancy.
Date conflicts between the bank and AP subledger are labeled Date discrepancy.
Withdrawals without an exact supported AP match are labeled Unmatched (no AP invoice for this amount).
Unmatched withdrawals include an investigation and conclusion in Notes.
Any proposed relation to a partial invoice is labeled as a hypothesis unless the source data confirms the allocation.
Vendor, amount, status, and date findings agree with the named input files.

rubrics.rubric: Does the AP aging schedule correctly cover the instructed Q1 USD open and partial invoices as of March 31, 2024?
criterion: The aging population is limited to Q1 2024 invoices.
The aging population is limited to Currency USD.
Every Open invoice in scope is included.
Every Partial invoice in scope is included.
Days past due are measured from the due date as of March 31, 2024.
Each invoice is assigned to Current/0–30, 31–60, 61–90, or 90+ days.
Bucket assignments are arithmetically correct.
The aging basis is stated.
Any unavailable remaining-balance detail for a Partial invoice is disclosed rather than invented.

rubrics.rubric: Does Q1_2024_Schedule_C_Expense_Summary.csv map the Q1 expense population to official 2024 Schedule C lines with complete control totals?
criterion: The CSV uses exactly the eight required columns.

The CSV states its Q1 currency scope and treatment: either all currencies are converted to USD with a cited, consistently applied conversion basis, or USD-only scope is used because the supplied files provide no exchange-rate basis and excluded non-USD activity is disclosed.
Every Q1 GL expense within the stated currency scope is included.
Each expense amount agrees with General_Ledger_Sample.xlsx.
Each ScheduleC_Line uses an official 2024 Schedule C line identifier.
Each ScheduleC_Category agrees with the selected line.
Any expense added through a supported adjusting entry is clearly distinguished from an original GL row.
A subtotal row is present for every used Schedule C line.
A grand total row is present.
Line subtotals reconcile to the mapped detail.
The grand total reconciles to the line subtotals.

rubrics.rubric: Does the Schedule C Draft reproduce the required 2024 Schedule C structure with source-grounded Q1 amounts that tie to the expense summary?
criterion: Part I contains Lines 1 through 7.
Gross receipts are derived from the Q1 accrual-accounting revenue records.
Cost of goods sold is reported on the appropriate Schedule C line.
Gross profit is arithmetically correct.
Other income is included when supported by the Q1 records.
Gross income is arithmetically correct.
Part II contains an amount on every applicable expense line.
Total expenses are arithmetically correct.
Net profit or loss is arithmetically correct.
Schedule C line amounts tie to Q1_2024_Schedule_C_Expense_Summary.csv.
Bank-reconciliation adjustments included for tax reporting are traceable to a supported journal entry.

rubrics.rubric: Does Q1_2024_Reconciliation_Exceptions.csv provide a complete, non-duplicative log of the discrepancies found and their materiality?
criterion: The CSV uses exactly the seven required columns.
Each distinct bank-reconciliation discrepancy has its own exception record.
Each distinct vendor-audit discrepancy has its own exception record.
Exception_ID values are unique.
Source_File identifies where the discrepancy was found.
Reference identifies the relevant source transaction or record.
Amount quantifies the discrepancy when an amount is available.
Resolution states the action taken or recommended.
Status is either Resolved or Unresolved.
The log supports the workbook's materiality ranking.

rubrics.rubric: Do the three deliverables have the required structure and remain internally consistent across reconciliation, AP, and tax reporting?
criterion: Q1_2024_Reconciliation_Workbook.xlsx contains the four required worksheets in the required order.
The worksheet names match the instructed names.
The two CSV deliverables use the exact instructed filenames.
AP conclusions are traceable through APID and the displayed AP source fields, and Schedule C conclusions use observable official 2024 line identifiers and matching category names.
Shared transaction references have consistent amounts across the workbook and exceptions log.
Schedule C totals agree between the workbook and expense-summary CSV.
No resolved item is contradicted by an unresolved treatment elsewhere without explanation.
